quote: Die Funktion $\zeta(s, x) = \sum \frac{x^n}{n^s}$ $(n = [-0-]1, 2, \dots)$ [-ist-] ge- nügt keiner bekannten Differentialgl.. Beweise
english: The function zeta(s, x) = sum x^n / n^s (n = 1, 2, ...) satisfies no known differential equation. Proofs
topic: The page discusses how hard it is to prove that a differential equation cannot be solved by a single quadrature, then asks how solids, liquids, gases, aether and electricity should be described under molecular theory using mean values and expansions in small parameters, and finally states that the function zeta(s,x) = sum x^n/n^s satisfies no known differential equation.

triage.modern_statement: Show that the polylogarithm (Jonquière function) ζ(s,x) = Σ_{n≥1} x^n/n^s, taken as an analytic function of the two variables s and x, is differentially transcendental (hypertranscendental). That means it satisfies no algebraic partial differential equation P(s, x, ζ, ∂ζ/∂s, ∂ζ/∂x, …) = 0 with P a nonzero polynomial. A related point: the functional equation x ∂ζ/∂x = ζ(s−1,x) shifts s, so it is a mixed differential-difference relation, not an algebraic PDE.
triage.answered_by: Hilbert stated this as a conjecture in his 1900 Paris ICM address 'Mathematische Probleme', in the remarks that come right after Problem 18. D. D. Mordukhai-Boltovskoi worked on the hypertranscendence of ζ(s,x) in 1914 (Izv. Politekh. Inst. Varsh. 2). The usual citation for the proof is A. Ostrowski, 'Über Dirichletsche Reihen und algebraische Differentialgleichungen', Math. Z. 8 (1920), 241–298.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's 1900 problem list says that ζ(s,x) probably satisfies no algebraic partial differential equation. The remark appears just after the 18th problem and points to the functional equation x ∂ζ/∂x = ζ(s−1,x).
In the same address Hilbert notes that ζ(s) satisfies no algebraic differential equation, using Hölder's theorem on Γ(x).
In 1920 Ostrowski proved Hilbert's assertion by showing that ζ(s,x) satisfies no algebraic differential equation.
An English translation of Ostrowski's Math. Z. 8 (1920) paper describes it as proving Hilbert's conjecture about ζ(x,s) = Σ x^n/n^s.

Mordukhai-Boltovskoi, 'On hypertranscendence of the function ζ(s,x)', Izv. Politekh. Inst. Varsh. 2 (1914), is cited next to Ostrowski 1920 in later work on differential independence of zeta functions.

triage.why: The diary entry matches, almost word for word, the conjecture Hilbert stated publicly in the 1900 Paris address, in the passage after Problem 18. It is not one of the 23 numbered problems; it is an accompanying remark. Ostrowski is cited as having proved it in 1920, and Mordukhai-Boltovskoi wrote on the same question in 1914. The search results don't show whether Hilbert meant algebraic differential equations by 'bekannten Differentialgl.', but that is the form he stated publicly. The broader topic, differential independence and hypertranscendence of zeta functions, Dirichlet series and L-functions, is still being studied. Examples are papers by Markus (2007), Lagarias and Li on the Lerch transcendent (arXiv 1506.06161), and a 2025 Proc. AMS paper on the independence of Dirichlet series.
